title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a 'carré' Q = (S, A, R), the combinatorial structure of a square. 𝒟 is its automorphism group, the dihedral group of order 8. Its centre {1, a} is generated by the antipodism a (rotation by π). There are two Klein four-subgroups V_S ≅ F_2^C and V_A ≅ F_2^D, and the cyclic subgroup 𝒟^+ ≅ Z/4 of rotations. C and D are the two 2-element sets of reflections in V_S and V_A. ω_Q is the 2-element set of generators of 𝒟^+, i.e. the orientations of the square.

The previous page showed that 𝒟/{1,a} = 𝒟_ab ≅ F_2 × F_2 carries a canonical basis. This page records the dictionary given by pull-back along 𝒟 → 𝒟_ab:
- the three lines F_2×0, 0×F_2 and the diagonal pull back to the three index-2 subgroups V_S, V_A and 𝒟^+;
- the three nonzero vectors (1,0), (0,1), (1,1) pull back to the three cosets C, D, ω_Q of the centre.

He then lists the elements of order 2: a, the two elements of C (each generating a coordinate line of V_S), and the two elements of D. The two elements of ω_Q have order 4. This gives the conjugacy-class decomposition 𝒟 = {1} ⊔ {a} ⊔ C ⊔ D ⊔ ω_Q: five orbits under Int(𝒟).

The complete list of proper nontrivial subgroups follows:
- three of order 4 (V_S, V_A, 𝒟^+), all normal;
- five of order 2: the centre, plus two pairs of non-normal reflection subgroups lying in V_S and V_A respectively.

The marginal note says the four non-central order-2 subgroups are not normal. Their normalizers are V_S and V_A, and the normal ones are V_S, V_A, 𝒟^+ and {1,a}.

The page ends by starting to list the canonical 2-element sets (F_2-torsors) attached to Q. On the next page this leads to ω_Q ∧ C ∧ D ≅ 1, i.e. the three Z/2-torsors C, D, ω_Q, being the fibres over the three nonzero points of 𝒟_ab, have trivial 'product'.

Purpose: in the context of moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, this is bookkeeping for level structures related to 2-/4-torsion. D_8 is the 2-Sylow of S_4 acting on the four branch points / 2-torsion points, i.e. the stabilizer of a pairing of a 4-set. The aim is to name canonically all the torsors and subgroups so that moduli of 'squares' can be described intrinsically, without choices.
errors: In the second brace the inverse images of (1,0) and (0,1) are written as 'C ⊂ 𝒟^+' and 'D ⊂ 𝒟^+' (if the transcription is right). C and D consist of reflections and lie in V_S and V_A, not in the rotation subgroup 𝒟^+; only ω_Q ⊂ 𝒟^+. Likely a slip of the pen or a misreading of '𝒟'.

Otherwise the group theory is correct: D_8 has five conjugacy classes and ten subgroups (1; five of order 2; three of order 4; 𝒟). The normalizers of the non-central reflection subgroups are the Klein groups containing them.

ideas.what: Lattice of subgroups and conjugacy classes of the dihedral group of order 8, described via the extension 1 → Z/2 → D_8 → F_2^2 → 1
ideas.modern_name: Subgroup lattice of D_4 (order 8); central extension of the Klein group

ideas.what: Canonical F_2-torsors (2-element sets) C, D, ω_Q attached to a square as fibres of D_8 → F_2^2 over nonzero vectors, with orientation torsor ω_Q
ideas.modern_name: Z/2-torsors / orientation torsors; fibres of a central extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; torsor yoga in the Grothendieck school

ideas.what: Choice-free ('canonical') description of the symmetry structure of a 4-element set with a square structure, for use with level structures on elliptic curves
ideas.modern_name: D_8 ⊂ S_4 as stabilizer of a pairing; level-2/4 structures, Legendre family

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, correct enumeration of the subgroups and conjugacy classes of D_8, done in Grothendieck's characteristic choice-free torsor style. It is bookkeeping toward a moduli description, with no new result or connection on this page.
transcription_corrections: The antipodism is written 'a' (centre {1,a}), consistent with the previous page, not 'ε'.
The second brace targets probably read 'C ⊂ 𝒟', 'D ⊂ 𝒟', 'ω_Q ⊂ 𝒟^+' (or the author wrote 𝒟^+ by slip); mathematically C, D ⊄ 𝒟^+.
'Les sous-groupes d'ordre deux de 𝒟 correspondent aux éléments d'ordre 2, il y a comme tels éléments' — 'correspondant' should be 'correspondent'.
The parenthetical reads 'NB les deux éléments de ω_Q sont d'ordre 4' or similar, rather than '3 éléments de 𝒟^+'.
The last line's first symbol (rendered 𝔹) is uncertain; possibly 𝒟 or another 2-element set; 'trois ensembles' may be 'divers ensembles'.
